This ratio, not an official SPDR-published per-share figure (spdrgoldshares.com's live ounces-per-share field returned 'AWAITING' on fetch), is what any GLD-equivalent conversion of a spot gold forecast would need to use.

case.value: The bulls' case for gold/GLD: persistent central-bank reserve diversification away from the dollar (Goldman models ~60 tonnes/month of EM central-bank buying) plus a resumption of ETF inflows (three straight monthly global inflow months into physically-backed gold ETFs through August 2026) should keep pushing spot gold toward the $4,900-$5,600/oz range major banks are forecasting for end-2026/2027.

depends_on.value: Central banks continuing to buy at a similar pace and real rates/the dollar not resuming a sustained uptrend; named bank targets: Goldman Sachs $4,900 by end-2026 and $5,400-$5,600 for 2027, J.P. Morgan and UBS both $5,400 by end-2027, Morgan Stanley's more conservative Q4 2026 base case of $4,800 (no explicit 2027 figure published)

bear_case.value: Spot gold fell to $4,420/oz on Sep 4, 2026 (-1.28% on the day) after a stronger-than-expected August jobs report lifted Treasury yields and the dollar and revived bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike, the classic headwind for a zero-yield asset like gold; a sustained real-rate/dollar rebound is the main risk to the forecasts above.

judgment.prospect_why: The case is central-bank buying of roughly 60 tonnes a month plus resumed ETF inflows carrying spot toward the published bank targets of $4,800 to $5,600 against $4,420 spot; the buying is observed rather than forecast, which is why this is mid-range and not lower.
judgment.competition_why: Scored as substitution risk to this vehicle rather than to the metal: GLD charges 0.40% against GLDM at 0.10% and IAU at 0.25% for the same exposure, so the incumbent is the expensive way to own the trade and steadily loses flow to its own cheaper clones.
judgment.macro_fit_why: Genuinely two-sided: the weaker dollar down 1.55%, 3.4% headline CPI and the accelerating oil and geopolitics shock support it, while a 2.42% real 10-year and a live September hike are the classic headwind, and the hawkish side is currently winning since spot fell 1.3% on the payrolls beat.
judgment.narrative_why: The debasement and geopolitics narrative is live and the Iran shock is accelerating, but its counter-narrative, the Fed hawkish pivot, is the theme the macro brief rates accelerating fastest and it is the one moving the price right now.
